content:
sasha: Heads-up — I repro a steady KV-cache memory growth on longctx runs that diverges on A100 vs H100. Looks like paged PT entries aren't being reclaimed when small fragments are reused.

maya: ugh. sequence length? batch? which model?

sasha: longctx test harness, seq=8192, batch=1, llama-ish 7B. Happens after ~45k tokens. A100 climbs to ~36GB cached, H100 stays ~22GB.

ben: can you paste the evict logs? any errors from the pager?

sasha: here's the relevant snippet from runtime logs after the leak starts:

```
KV_PAGER: pin page id=0x7f3b1a, frag=3 owner=worker-12
KV_PAGER: evict try page=0x7f3b1a flags=LRU
EVICT: page 0x7f3b1a -> enqueue, mapped=1, refcount=0
KV_PT: remap slot=42 -> phys=0x8a00 (sparse remap)
KV_PT: frag 3 reuse -> mark stale=true but keep PTE
WARN: PT_STALE_KEEP mapping_count=1 frag=3
```

sasha: the suspicious line is "mark stale=true but keep PTE" — on A100 we then later reassign that slot to a new frag but the old PTE never gets cleared. H100 path seems to clear it.

maya: does the kernel selection differ? A100 uses our old fused kernel for paged attention, H100 uses the new tiled kernel. Could be a different eviction sequence.

ben: interesting. I can try to reproduce with tiled kernel on A100. Meanwhile, try disabling sparse remap to see if it regresses to no leak.

alex: @ben also check PCI ordering: A100 test infra has PCIe 3 interconnect, H100 has NVLink. Remap ordering races could show only on one interconnect.

ben: repro cmd I'm running locally:

```bash
python tests/longctx_run.py --model=7B --seq=8192 --batch=1 --kernels=paged,tiled --pager-log-level=debug
```

ben: initial perf flame shows lots of time in pagewalk and kernel memcpy on A100 after 20k tokens. On H100 the pagewalk is short and we see more coalesced writes.

sasha: attaching a minimal heap map (summarized):

- A100: PT entries total=121k, stale=18k, frag-count skewed to small fragments (avg frag pages=2.2)
- H100: PT entries total=84k, stale=1.2k, avg frag pages=5.1

maya: small fragments piling up could explain fragmentation. The reclaim path batches clears by frag id — if a frag is reused before reclaim completes, we may leave orphaned PTEs. That matches "mark stale but keep PTE".

alex: could be our atomic state machine for frag lifecycle has a hole. If frag reuse races with reclaim finalizer, the finalizer might skip freeing PTEs. NVLink fast mem ops hide the timing on H100.

ben: I added extra asserts in the finalizer and ran under TSAN-ish instrumentation. On A100 I hit: "finalizer: expected owner==reclaimer but got owner==worker-12"

sasha: exact repro steps/timeframe?

ben: ~37 minutes into the longctx run with seq=8192. Consistent on our A100 farm.

maya: temporary mitigation: force eviction to wait for finalizer completion before reassigning a slot. That should avoid double-ownership races. Can we hotpatch that in canary?

alex: ops-bot, can we schedule a canary with the mitigation on the A100 pool only? Don't roll to H100 for now.

ops-bot: deploy request queued: canary "kv-pager/finalizer-wait" -> target: cluster-a100-canary. ETA 12m. :eyes:

sasha: thanks. if canary looks good we'll run longer (6h) to confirm no growth. Also want a perf trace pre/post to confirm no regression in tail latency.

ben: follow-ups I plan:
- add logging for frag lifecycle transitions (allocate, pin, mark_stale, finalizer_free)
- test tiled kernel on A100 to isolate kernel ordering impact
- run with sparse-remap off to confirm gap

sasha: perfect. Also check for related driver warnings — I saw occasional "GPU page table invalidation delayed" in dmesg on A100 node. Could be compounding.

maya: noted. I'll grep node logs. If driver invalidation is delayed, extending finalizer wait might be required (ugly but safe).

alex: last thing — add a repro harness that forces worst-case: many small fragments reused rapidly (frag size=1 page). That should amplify the race if it's there.

sasha: putting a link to the local run logs: https://internal/logs/2002345678/kv-leak-a100 (private)

ben: will post PR for the finalizer-wait branch once I have tests. low-risk change, should be quick.

sasha: thanks all. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
